newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer proposes to convert K-shrs to A-shrs.
newsitem.headline: Amer proposes to convert K-shrs to A-shrs.

text.p: Finnish sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said in a statement on Tuesday it will propose to an extraordinary shareholders' meeting on June 2 that all its unlisted K-shares be converted into listed A-shares.
Amer proposed to implement the conversion by redeeming all K-shares at a ratio of 1.2 A-shares for each K-share.

"The technical implementation will entail redemption of all K shares by decreasing the share capital," Amer said, adding it would redeem K-shares for 24 markka each and that the subscription price for A-shares would be 20 markka per share.
Amer said the move would improve the share's liquidity.
After the conversion, "Amer will have only one publicly listed share series, and all shares will carry equal voting rights," it said.
The company's four big K-shareholders had undertaken to subscribe A-shares of an equivalent value to their current holdings under a private placement, Amer said.
K-shares carry 100 times the voting power of A-shares, and the company's four K-shareholders together have exercised absolute control at annual general meetings, Amer said.

The proposed new structure would mean that A-shares will account for 100 percent of shares and votes. Those holding A-shares now will see their share of the total votes boosted to 87 percent from 9.5 percent, the company said.

"The trend among investors has for some time been towards clearly structured share series, and international investors in particular value a structure where no group of shareholders is in a dominant position," Amer said.
A more transparent ownership structure was also expected to "improve the ability to use the A shares to raise equity finance and as a payment for eventual acquisitions," it added.

The entire K series is held by the company's four founding shareholders: The Finnish Association of Graduate Engineers TEK, The Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration, KY; The Finnish Association of Graduates in Economics and Business Administration, SEFE; and The Land and Water Technology Foundation.
About a year ago, the K-shareholders said they had been approached by a potential buyer, but no deal ever took place.
Under the proposed scheme, their voting rights would fall to 13 percent from over 90 percent while their shareholding would ease to 87 percent from 88.5 percent, Amer said.

"Today the only way for K shareholders to realise any part of their shareholdings is to sell control in the company. If the K shares are exchanged for A shares, this will improve the liquidity of the K shareholdings thus reducing the risk of sudden major changes in the ownership base of Amer," it said. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, news@reuters.fi
